items.evidence: RTM: catalogue pack/read + category-policy wired; product duplicate-detection wired (POST /v1/catalogue/products/duplicates); product-master WRITE PATH wired (POST /v1/catalogue/products/:id/publish behind the compliance gate + GET reads, event-sourced latest-per-id, integration-tested); barcode register WRITE PATH wired (POST /v1/catalogue/products/:id/barcodes/:code enforcing one-code-one-item via the tested BarcodeRegistry + lookup/list reads, event-sourced, integration-tested); tax-class GST-RATE SCHEDULE wired (POST /v1/catalogue/tax-classes/:hsn/rates/:date via the tested resolveGstRate, per-HSN effective-dated, one-rate-per-date, + resolve/list reads, integration-tested); catalogue-pack ASSEMBLY + SIGNED PUBLISH now wired (GET /v1/catalogue/pack/preview folds product master + prices + barcodes + tax rates into one snapshot for a store, AND POST /v1/catalogue/pack now BUILDS the signed pack from that same fold — an authored+priced+barcoded+taxed product reaches the lane on the signed pack it reads, an unpriced one is never shipped; integration-tested end to end incl. the shrink guard); product-authoring SCREEN write path underway (slices 1-2: the tested ProductPublishRequested outbox command + the shell Publish button now commits it to a DEVICE-backed catalogue outbox via catalogue-session.requestPublish — Save validates then durably queues, no network from the screen; unit-tested); product-publish delivery per owner decision ADR-0013 (signed-in operator delivers, not a service identity) — slice 1 the tested review-queue classifier + slice 2 the tested operator-session delivery (deliverReadyPublishes sends only ready items via an injected operator-auth port to the idempotent publish route, acknowledging/holding/dead-lettering on result, no auto-publish) + slice 3 the tested review-queue SCREEN session model (createProductPublishReviewSession presents the whole outbox incl. visible dead-letters/published items, each with a live word+icon state re-evaluated from the operator's CURRENT context, attention-first ordering, plain-English exception guidance, bilingual EN/TA, a nobody-named refusal, and a SEPARATE deliver() action delegating to slice 2 — no auto-publish on view/login) + slice 4 the SHELL + edge wiring (web/product-publish-review.html+.js opens offline via the shared web-erp SW, draws rows + a Publish button that runs ONLY on an explicit click; browser-entry boots it over the SAME device-backed catalogue outbox the Save commits to, with a concrete operator-session delivery port POSTing to the idempotent publish route under credentials:'same-origin' — the operator's own auth cookie, never a service token; registered as a served screen with PackProductPublishReviewPolicy feeding only the operator's CURRENT context re-read each render, menu gated catalogue.pack.publish; usability guardrail + offline e2e + screen-feed tests) + slice 5 the CENTRAL-BOUNDARY re-checks + audit (the cloud publish route trusts no client verdict: re-runs the tested publishProduct compliance gate AND adds SKU uniqueness across the whole tenant — a SKU held by a DIFFERENT product is refused 409 sku_already_in_use, nothing overwritten, while same-product re-publish is a legitimate new version; audit attribution [ADR-0013 control 10] is already provided by the kernel — a SHA-256-sealed append-only audit_log row per write and per refusal, naming the AUTHENTICATED userId, FND-02) + slice 6 the BARCODE-ASSIGNMENT leg of delivery (the command carries each barcode as {code,kind} — the symbology is a real authoring fact, never guessed; deliverOnePublish publishes the product FIRST then assigns each barcode on the one-code-one-item route under the operator's own session, collapsing to one outbox status — a real barcode conflict dead-letters, a transient failure holds+retries idempotently, all-in acknowledges; also corrected the delivery classifier so a 409 is a REAL conflict → dead-letter, not a mistaken idempotent-success) + slice 7 the BROWSER E2E MATRIX (a real headless-Chromium test seeds the device outbox with a queued publish, injects the operator context, and drives the actual screen: an authorised operator's Publish sends the product-master POST then the barcode POST and the queue clears; a no-permission operator's button is disabled and nothing is sent; a 409 barcode conflict dead-letters — the ADR-0013 delivery chain is now fully E2E-verified end to end; this first real browser RUN also caught + fixed a defect the CI-skipped e2e had hidden — product-publish-review.js was missing from the service-worker SHELL cache so the screen did not truly open offline, now added + cache bumped v13→v14) landed; the §28 REVERSIBLE MERGE-WRITE is now WIRED too (M03-WIRE inc-A: POST /v1/catalogue/merges/:id PROPOSES [catalogue.merge.propose], POST …/decision APPROVES-or-rejects [the distinct catalogue.merge.approve, mirroring the price propose/approve split] with the tested mergeProducts refusing a self-approval on two SERVER-attributed identities so proposer≠approver per §28 even for an owner holding both codes, POST …/reverse undoes it as a reversible LINK never a deletion [hard rule #2], GET /v1/catalogue/products/:id/canonical resolves a merged id via resolveProductId; event-sourced MergeProposed→MergeApproved/MergeRejected→MergeReversed [rejections/reversals kept, hard rule #6], integration-tested 9 cases incl. a cold-restart rebuild). The SECOND tested engine is now WIRED too (M03-WIRE inc-B): POST /v1/catalogue/products/:id/pack DEFINES a product pack ladder (unit->inner->case) behind the tested validatePack — an inexact pack (non-integer count of the level below, base level != one base unit, two levels sharing a name, or none) is refused 422 pack_hierarchy_is_not_exact at DEFINITION time, before it can make a stock figure wrong at the back door; GET .../pack reads it; GET .../pack/convert?level=&quantity=&direction=to-base|from-base runs the tested toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits/conversionIsReversible (2 cases -> 48 base units exactly; 50 base units -> 2 whole cases + 2 singles, never a fraction of a case); event-sourced PackHierarchyDefined latest-per-product [hard rule #2], integration-tested 8 cases incl. a cold-restart rebuild. RE-RATED to WIRED (owner-ratified Option A, 19 Aug): both ENGINE_ONLY M03 engines the re-assessment named — reversible merge (inc-A) + pack/UOM conversion (inc-B) — are now live on the API, on top of the already-wired+integration-tested product-truth core (FR-01 authoring, FR-02 barcode identity, FR-03 tax/MRP/allergen/recall) and the E2E-verified ADR-0013 operator-publish chain. Remaining M03 follow-ons (NOT blocking WIRED, the path onward to INTEGRATION_TESTED/E2E for the whole module): images + bulk-edit (FR-04), a category-delete-with-stock guard, and EmbeddedBarcodeRule weight/price-embedded parse (D01-attributed, a separate denominator item).

items.evidence: RTM: supplier/procurement — bank-change verification recorded as an event (D03-FR-06 wired). PO ISSUE + SUPPLIER-BLOCK + OPEN-COMMITMENT now WIRED on API-03 (M06-WIRE inc-1, M06-FR-01/02/04): POST /v1/purchase/orders/:poId PROPOSES a PO (gated purchase.order.propose, requisitioner = the authenticated buyer), POST .../approval APPROVES+ISSUES it via the tested decide()+issuePurchaseOrder — the approver cannot be the requisitioner (§28 enforced by identity even when one user holds both codes → 409 proposer_cannot_approve) and a blocked supplier is refused (409 supplier_blocked); the hold is its own append-only latest-wins record (POST /v1/purchase/suppliers/:id/block-status, gated purchase.supplier.block); GET /v1/purchase/commitments now runs the tested computeOpenCommitment over the issued POs, flipping from not-known to a real figure (still not-known, not zero, until the first PO exists); event-sourced PurchaseOrderProposed/PurchaseOrderIssued/SupplierBlockStatusSet, restart-safe, integration-tested 6 cases. SUPPLIER SCORECARDS + CONTRACT ALERTS now WIRED too (M06-WIRE inc-2, M06-FR-03): POST /v1/purchase/suppliers/:supplierId/receipts/:poId records a delivery OUTCOME per PO (gated purchase.performance.record, latest-per-PO so a correction supersedes and the score counts a delivery once), POST /v1/purchase/contracts/:contractId records a contract (gated purchase.contract.manage, latest-per-id), GET /v1/purchase/suppliers/:supplierId/scorecard runs the tested scoreSupplier over the recorded facts + the active contract (fill rate, on-time vs contracted lead time, lead-time RELIABILITY from the spread, price adherence, quality, weighted overall, worst-signal-first summary, not_rated where there is no evidence), GET /v1/purchase/contracts/alerts runs reviewContracts (expiring/expired/UNAPPROVED worst-first); event-sourced SupplierReceiptRecorded/SupplierContractRecorded, restart-safe, integration-tested 7 cases. PO AMEND/CANCEL/RECEIPT + open-commitment NETTING now WIRED too (M06-WIRE inc-3, M06-FR-04): POST /v1/purchase/orders/:poId/amendments amends an issued PO's lines (gated purchase.order.approve, keeps the prior lines on the ledger, re-prices), .../cancellations records an approved per-product cancellation, .../receipts posts received qty per product (gated purchase.order.receive, in the PO's ordering units); computeOpenCommitment now nets ordered − received − cancelled and GET /v1/purchase/commitments follows; amend/cancel/receive refused on a non-issued PO (409 purchase_order_not_issued), each idempotent on its own id (no double-count); event-sourced PurchaseOrderAmended/PurchaseOrderCancelled/PurchaseOrderReceiptPosted, restart-safe, integration-tested (12 cases total). REBATES now WIRED too (M06-WIRE inc-4, M06-FR-03 / M23): POST /v1/purchase/rebate-schemes/:schemeId records a scheme (gated purchase.contract.manage, latest-per-id), POST .../accruals/:accrualId runs the tested accrueRebate (nothing accrues below threshold and it says how far short, a growth scheme measures against baseline, outstanding = accrued − received is the earned-not-claimed headline, latest-per-accrualId so a re-measure/payment supersedes), GET .../accruals totals accrued/received/outstanding; event-sourced RebateSchemeRecorded/RebateAccrued, restart-safe, integration-tested 6 cases. HELD at PARTIALLY_WIRED (owner directive 'wire the two, hold M06'): the ONE remaining M06 gap is requisition/RFQ/quotation-comparison (UNBUILT — no engine exists, needs building not wiring), so M06 is deliberately not re-rated to WIRED. FR-01/02/03/04 all now have live paths; the finance-side rebate-claim APPROVAL (M23) is a separate follow-on.
